Therefore, TiO 2 is ﬁrst reduced by the 7075 Al alloy matrix to Ti and formed by MgO at the interface.
C element from CF diffuses into the 7075 Al alloy matrix during the sintering process causing C element to react with Ti element limited by MgO generating TiC.
Crack in the 7075 Al alloy matrix is guided by the Al 4C3 on the interface between CF and the 7075 Al alloy matrix. Crack cuts CF directly due to poor shear resistance of CF.

When the crack extends near the interface between matrix and ﬁber, the crack propagation path is deﬂected. Same deﬂection of cracks was found in other composites with ﬁbers [ 35]. In the process of crack propagation along the interface, the matrix is separated from the ﬁber surface, but the ﬁber always bears tensile stress and ﬁnally breaks.

The interface layer can separate Al 4C3 and CF, preventing direct crack propagation from Al 4C3 to CF and resulting in direct cutting off of CF. Deﬂection of cracks at the interface effectively reduces the shear failure proportion and increases the tensile failure proportion of CF.
